display_name: Black Box Deep & Dark Cabernet Sauvignon, California
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Black Box Deep & Dark Cabernet Sauvignon packs blackcurrant and dark chocolate punch from California fruit into a 3-liter box that stays fresh for weeks after opening. Gold medal at 2022 competitions proves it overdelivers for $20. Bag-in-box tech blocks oxygen, explaining the consistent quality.",
  "wine_summary": "Black Box built its name on affordable boxed wines that rival bottled equivalents in fruit depth. This Deep & Dark edition sources Cabernet across California for a ripe, approachable profile that earned bronze through gold medals in TEXSOM and other awards. Producers like Black Box prioritize volume and value, blending sites to hit black plum and cedar notes reliably every vintage.",
  "terroir_expression": "California table wine status means no fixed soils or sites, but warm-climate sourcing drives the ripe blackcurrant and plush dark cherry here—long sunny seasons extend hang time for fruit concentration over green pepper herbal notes. Expect softer tannins from heat-ripened grapes, contrasting cooler Cab zones like Coonawarra.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fruit undergoes cool fermentation in stainless steel to lock in cassis aromas, followed by brief oak contact for tobacco and graphite layers. Extended maceration softens thick-skinned Cabernet tannins, key for box-ready drinkability. Boxing in nitrogen-flushed bags halts oxidation, letting flavors hold six weeks post-tap.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken: spice meets grippy tannins and dark fruit acidity to balance heat. Cheeseburger with cheddar: juicy beef fat clings to plush texture while blackcurrant cuts through. Braised short ribs: slow-cooked richness pairs with cedar depth and soft structure. Spaghetti bolognese: tomato acidity syncs with wine's medium tannins. Grilled pork chops with chimichurri: herbal sauce amplifies green pepper hints.",
  "comparable_wines": "Bota Box Cabernet Sauvignon — same boxed format, ripe California fruit at $18, softer body. [yellow tail] Cabernet Sauvignon — budget bottled rival with similar black plum ripeness under $10. Josh Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon — comparable dark chocolate notes from Paso Robles at $15.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with soft tannins and ripe black fruit",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink now through 2025; store box upright in cool dark spot. No bottle cellaring needed—box format limits long-term aging.",
  "value_assessment": "$19.99 for 3 liters on Enofile. Bota Box Cabernet ($18) and Dark Horse Cabernet ($15) compete directly. Strong buy for volume and medal-winning depth that beats most sub-$20 bottles per liter.",
  "market_position": "Supermarket shelves target casual weeknight cooks and barbecue hosts seeking no-fuss red. Party planners stock it for crowds, avoiding cork drama. Rarely on restaurant lists, but home entertainers value the freshness edge.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if chasing terroir nuance—this blends power over precision. People dismiss boxed Cab as low-end, missing how it crushes parties better than pricier bottles that fade fast. Buy for value-driven steak nights, ignore for collectors.",
  "aging_potential_years": null,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 0,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 3,
  "sensory": {

  }
}
